tool.name: BAM Readcount
tool.description: Generate metrics at single nucleotide positions
tool.command:
#if $input_bam.is_of_type('cram') #set $alignment = 'input.cram' ln -s '$input_bam' input.cram && ln -s '$input_bam.metadata.cram_index' input.cram.crai && #else #set $alignment = 'input.bam' ln -s '$input_bam' input.bam && ln -s '$input_bam.metadata.bam_index' input.bam.bai && #end if
#if $reference_fasta.is_of_type('fasta.gz') gunzip -c '$reference_fasta' > reference.fa && #else ln -s '$reference_fasta' reference.fa && #end if
#if $target.target_select == 'site_list' #if $target.coordinates == 'bed' ## BED is 0-based and half-open, a bam-readcount site list is 1-based and end-inclusive awk 'BEGIN{FS = OFS = "\t"} NF >= 3 && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ {print $1, $2 + 1, $3}' '$target.site_list' > site_list.tsv && #else ln -s '$target.site_list' site_list.tsv && #end if #else if $target.target_select == 'region' ## bam-readcount silently ignores a region without an end coordinate and reports ## the whole file instead, so 'chr1:42' is expanded to 'chr1:42-42' here #set $region = str($target.region).strip() #set $region_parts = $region.split(':') #if len($region_parts) == 2 and '-' not in $region_parts[1] #set $region = $region_parts[0] + ':' + $region_parts[1] + '-' + $region_parts[1] #end if #end if
bam-readcount --reference-fasta reference.fa --min-mapping-quality $advanced.min_mapping_quality --min-base-quality $advanced.min_base_quality --max-count $advanced.max_count --max-warnings $advanced.max_warnings $advanced.per_library $advanced.insertion_centric #if $target.target_select == 'site_list' --site-list site_list.tsv #end if $alignment #if $target.target_select == 'region' '$region' #end if > '$output'

param.name: input_bam
param.label: Alignment file
param.help: Coordinate-sorted and indexed BAM or CRAM file.

param.label: Reference FASTA
param.help: Reference sequence the alignment file was mapped against. It is used to report the reference base at each position and to decode CRAM input.

param.name: target_select
param.label: Restrict counting to
param.help: By default every position covered by at least one read is reported.
param.option: A single region typed in below

param.name: region
param.label: Region
param.help: Samtools-style region: a reference name alone (chr1), a single 1-based position (chr1:42) or a 1-based, end-inclusive range (chr1:42-99).

validator.message: Use chr, chr:position or chr:start-end, for example chr1, chr1:42 or chr1:42-99

param.label: Region file
param.help: Tabular file without header listing one region per line as reference name, start and end.

param.name: coordinates
param.label: Coordinate convention of the region file
param.help: Pick the convention that matches the file, the two differ by one base in the start coordinate.
param.option: BED: 0-based start, end-exclusive (converted on the fly)

param.label: Minimum mapping quality
param.help: Reads with a lower MAPQ are not counted.

param.label: Minimum base quality
param.help: Bases with a lower quality are not counted.

param.label: Maximum depth
param.help: Pileup depth at which counting stops, to keep memory usage bounded.

param.label: Report per library
param.help: Report one block of counts per read group library instead of one block per position.

param.label: Insertion centric
param.help: Report insertion counts. Reads carrying an insertion are then excluded from the per-base counts.

param.label: Maximum warnings per type
param.help: bam-readcount writes a warning to the job log whenever it skips malformed input, for example a region outside the reference or an unparsable site list line. This caps how often each kind of warning is repeated so that a broken input does not flood the log. 0 suppresses the warnings, -1 prints all of them.

tool.help:
**BAM Readcount**
Generates low-level metrics at single nucleotide positions from a BAM or CRAM file. Reported metrics include the observed bases, read counts, mapping and base qualities, strandedness, mismatch counts and the position of the base within the reads.
The tool was originally written to help filter genomic mutation calls, but the metrics are equally useful as input for variant detection tools and for resolving disagreements between variant callers.
-----
**Inputs**
*Alignment file* Coordinate-sorted and indexed BAM or CRAM file.
*Reference FASTA* Reference sequence the reads were mapped against, plain or gzipped. It provides the reference base reported for each position and is also used to decode CRAM input.
*Restrict counting to* By default every position covered by at least one read is reported. Counting can instead be limited either to a single region typed into the form or to a set of regions read from a file.
A typed region uses samtools syntax and 1-based, end-inclusive coordinates: ``chr1`` for a whole reference sequence, ``chr1:42`` for a single position or ``chr1:42-99`` for a range.
A region file holds one region per line as three tab-separated columns. Note that a bam-readcount site list is **not** a BED file: its start coordinate is 1-based and its end coordinate is inclusive, so the site list line ``chr1 10 12`` covers the same three bases as the BED line ``chr1 9 12``. Select the matching convention next to the file and BED input is converted automatically.
-----
**Output**
A tabular file with one line per reported position::
chr position ref_base depth base_data [base_data ...]
Each ``base_data`` field is a colon-separated record for one of the possible bases (``=``, ``A``, ``C``, ``G``, ``T``, ``N``)::
base:count:avg_mapping_quality:avg_basequality:avg_se_mapping_quality:num_plus_strand:num_minus_strand:avg_pos_as_fraction:avg_num_mismatches_as_fraction:avg_sum_mismatch_qualities:num_q2_containing_reads:avg_distance_to_q2_start_in_q2_reads:avg_clipped_length:avg_distance_to_effective_3p_end
With **Report per library** enabled, each line instead carries one ``library_name { ... }`` block per read-group library.
-----
**Advanced Options**
*Minimum mapping quality* Reads below this MAPQ are ignored (default: 0).
*Minimum base quality* Bases below this quality are ignored (default: 0).
*Maximum depth* Depth at which counting stops, which bounds memory usage (default: 10,000,000).
*Report per library* Break the counts down by read-group library.
*Insertion centric* Report insertion counts. Reads carrying an insertion are then left out of the per-base counts.
*Maximum warnings per type* bam-readcount warns whenever it skips malformed input, such as a region outside the reference or a site list line it cannot parse. This setting caps how often each kind of warning is repeated so a broken input cannot flood the job log. The default of 0 suppresses the warnings, -1 prints all of them.
